content:
Attorneys for Sean ‘Diddy’ Combs filed a motion to drop him as a client on Monday over unpaid legal fees and a lack of cooperation.

The motion was filed in his case against Nexstar Media, Ariel Mitchell and Courtney Burgess in which he claims they wrongly reported that Combs mixed drugs with baby oil on NewsNation’s “Banfield.”

One of his attorneys, Michael Tremonte, partner at Sher Tremonte LLP, explained in a court document that Combs has not paid a “substantial” amount of his legal fees and has been “unreasonably difficult” to work with.

More specifically, Tremonte said Combs’ latest payment for their legal services was provided in late 2025, and he has also failed to make “himself available for timely, substantive, and direct communications about his cases for over four months.”

They are also seeking a retaining lien against the hip-hop mogul until all fees are paid in full.

By contrast, Combs claimed through a spokesperson that he chose to sever ties with the attorneys because he was being overcharged.

“I made the decision to switch lawyers because I won’t let anyone take advantage of me by overcharging me and running up bills that were never approved. This is strictly a business matter, and any talk about unpaid fees is just part of our dispute over those unapproved charges,” Combs told HuffPost through his spokesperson, Juda Engelmayer.

Tremonte told Rolling Stone the attorneys “represented Mr. Combs zealously and very efficiently under challenging circumstances. As stated in our court filings, we are withdrawing from representing him because he has not paid his long-overdue invoices and has become uncooperative. Any suggestion that we overcharged him is simply false.”

Combs is serving out a 50-month sentence at Federal Correctional Institution, Fort Dix in New Jersey after being convicted on two counts of transportation to engage in prostitution. The disgraced hip-hop star has been accused of sexual assault, violence and creating a toxic working environment in dozens of lawsuits since 2023.

In November 2023, his ex-girlfriend, singer and model Casandra ‘Cassie’ Ventura, filed a damning suit accusing him of domestic violence and rape. Her lawsuit was quickly settled, but it set off a chain reaction of dozens of other accusers stepping forward with their own allegations against Combs.

Combs and Sher Tremonte, respectively, did not immediately respond to HuffPost’s requests for comment.
